Client for app-update-server (github.com/mcanyucel/app-update-server): checks for a newer version, downloads its installer, verifies its SHA-256 and runs it silently. No UI; see Bridgewiz.AppUpdate.Avalonia for the dialog.

Update dialog and check flows for Avalonia desktop apps using Bridgewiz.AppUpdate: a quiet check at startup, Help > Check for updates, release notes, download progress, skip this version, and a silent install that reopens the app.
AWS transport for Olax.Messaging: one SNS topic fanned out to one SQS queue per service, filtered by event name, with a redrive dead-letter queue.
Azure Event Hubs transport for Olax.Messaging. Runs the Kafka transport against the namespace's Kafka endpoint (Standard tier and above), configured from just the namespace connection string.
Azure Service Bus transport for Olax.Messaging: one topic, one subscription per service with a correlation rule per event, and the built-in dead-letter queue.

Transactional outbox and inbox for OLAX messaging on the service's EF Core DbContext (PostgreSQL / Npgsql): events commit with the business change and each event is handled once. Registers everything with AddOlaxMessaging<TDbContext>().
Google Cloud Pub/Sub transport for Olax.Messaging: a topic per event, a subscription per service and event, dead-letter topics, and native push to Cloud Run with OIDC verification.

Kafka transport for Olax.Messaging (also the engine of Olax.Messaging.Azure.EventHubs): three topics (events, retry, dead-letter), a consumer group per service, retries and dead letters built on topics.
RabbitMQ transport for Olax.Messaging: a topic exchange, one quorum queue per service, publisher confirms and a dead-letter queue.

Broker-neutral core of OLAX messaging: the message envelope, delivery rules, the transport abstraction and the relay endpoints. Add an outbox package (Olax.Messaging.EntityFrameworkCore) and a transport package for your broker.
Integration event contracts for OLAX services: IntegrationEvent, IEventPublisher and IIntegrationEventHandler. No EF Core or broker dependency, so the Application layer can reference it.
